title: Protocol to isolate mature thymic T cell subsets using fluorescence-activated cell sorting for assessing gene expression by RNA-seq and transcription factor binding across the genome by CUT and RUN
protocol: Label unwanted cells such as double positive (DP) cells with biotinylated antibodies.
Incubate the labeled cell mixture with streptavidin magnetic beads.
Place the sample on a magnetic stand for separation.
Remove and collect the supernatant containing mature thymic subsets.
Harvest the thymus from a euthanized mouse.
Place the thymus into a 6-well plate containing 3 mL TCM and put the plate on ice.
Transfer the thymus using clean forceps onto a 70 μm cell strainer in a p-60 plate.
Add 3 mL TCM to the thymus.
Gently dissociate the organ by using the end of the plunger of a 1 ml syringe without a needle.
Remove the cell strainer carefully to avoid discarding medium containing cells.
Transfer the TCM containing the thymocytes to a polystyrene tube.
Pipette the cells thoroughly at least ten times to achieve single-cell suspension.
Count the cells.
Transfer 10 μL of the sample to 90 μL PBS for counting in a flow cytometer.
Prepare a 1:10 dilution of the cells and add Trypan blue.
Count the cells using a Neubauer hemocytometer.
Resuspend the cells in FACS buffer to achieve a concentration of 1*10^8 cells per mL.
Transfer the cells to a polystyrene round-bottom tube.
Resuspend cells in FACS buffer within the specified volume range for the magnet type used (0.1-2 mL for standard tubes, 8.5 mL for larger magnets).
Add 50 μL of Rat Serum that has reached 22°C to 1 mL of FACS buffer containing 100 million cells.
Carefully mix the solution after adding Rat Serum.
For 1.5 mL of FACS buffer with 150 million thymocytes, add 75 μL Rat serum and carefully mix.
Add 3 μg/mL of biotinylated anti-CD24 antibody to the mixture.
Add 1 μg/mL anti-Ter119 to label erythrocytes.
Mix well after adding the antibodies.
Incubate the sample at 22°C for 10 minutes.
Bind labeled cells with biotinylated antibodies to magnetic streptavidin beads.
Add 100 μL RapidSpheres per mL of sample.
Mix and incubate at 22°C for 2.5 min.
Resuspend thoroughly the magnetic streptavidin RapidSpheres by vortexing them for 30 s before use.
Ensure the solution is homogeneous before aspirating the desired volume of beads.
Attach the beads and bound cells to the magnet.
Add FACS buffer up to 2.5 mL to each tube.
Mix by pipetting 2–3 times.
Place the tube on the magnet (without the cap) and incubate for 2.5 min.
Collect the supernatant containing unbound, enriched CD24- mature thymic subsets.
Count the collected cells.
Keep the cell sample on ice while preparing for the next steps.
Prepare a master mix in FACS buffer before use.
Stain up to 3 million cells in 100 μL of antibody master mix in a 1.5 mL tube.
Incubate the stained cells at 4°C for 30 minutes.
Wash cells two times with ice cold FACS buffer.
Centrifuge the cells for 5 minutes at 453 × g at 4°C.
Carefully discard the supernatant using a P1000 pipette, ensuring not to disturb the pellet.
Resuspend cells in 500 μL FACS buffer.
Centrifuge the cells for 5 minutes at 453 × g at 4°C.
Repeat steps i-iv once more.
Resuspend in appropriate volume to achieve a concentration of 10 × 10^6 cells/mL in FACS buffer.
Filter cells using a round bottom tube with cell strainer cap.
Centrifuge the sorted cells for 5 minutes at 453 × g at 4°C after sorting.
Prepare collection tubes containing FBS (or other collection medium of choice).
Pre-chill the adaptor for the collection tubes to keep sorted cells continuously at 4°C.
During sorting, record approximately 5,000 events from the sample.
Gate thymocytes based on forward and side scatter properties.
Exclude doublets and select single cells from the gated population.
Determine live cells by staining with viability discrimination dye and exclude dead cells.
Identify iNKT cells as aGalCer-CD1d tetramer positive and TCRβ intermediate cells.
Gating on TCRβ positive, aGalCer-CD1d tetramer negative cells to identify CD8 SP and CD4 SP cells based on surface expression of CD4 and CD8.
Sort for the desired mature thymic subsets such as CD4 SP cells.
Run a small amount of sorted sample (5,000 events) post-sorting to assess purity and cell viability.
Isolate total RNA.
Prepare libraries using the SMART-seq v4 Ultra Low Input RNA kit protocol for sequencing.
Optimize the number of PCR amplification cycles based on the starting RNA material to ensure adequate yield and complexity of the library.
Count the cells to obtain a precise quantification of the retrieved material.
Pellet the cells by centrifugation at 200 × g at 4°C for 5 minutes.
Wash the cells once with ice-cold PBS.
Centrifuge the cells again at 200 × g at 4°C.
Work on a dedicated clean bench or clean room if available.
Clean the bench and pipettes with RNase ZAP if working outside a clean environment.
Resuspend thoroughly the cell pellet in 350 μL RLT plus containing 10 μL of β mercaptoethanol just before RNA isolation.
Transfer the material to a DNA eliminating column.
Centrifuge at speed higher than 8,000 × g for 30 s at 22°C.
Discard the column and save the flow-through.
Add equal volume of 70% ethanol to the flow-through and mix carefully using a 1 mL pipette.
Transfer the mixture (700 μL) to a new RNA isolation column.
Centrifuge at 9,600 × g for 30 s.
Discard the flow-through.
Wash the column with 700 μL RW1 buffer.
Centrifuge at 9,600 × g for 30 s.
Discard the flow-through.
Wash with 500 μL ERP buffer.
Centrifuge at 9,600 × g for 30 s.
Discard the flow-through.
Repeat the wash with 500 μL of 80% ethanol.
Discard the flow-through.
Place the column in a new clean collection tube.
Centrifuge at maximum speed for 5 minutes.
Dry the membrane before eluting the RNA.
Place the dried column into a new 1.5 mL certified DNase/RNase-free tube.
Apply 13 μL of RNase free water directly to the membrane.
Incubate for 1 minute.
Centrifuge at maximum speed for 1 minute.
Discard the column.
Store the RNA at -80°C until further analysis.
Thaw the RNA samples when ready for quality control.
Quantify using Qubit RNA High Sensitivity (HS) Assay kit in a Qubit Fluorometer 4.
Assess RNA integrity using an Agilent High Sensitivity RNA screen tape and reagents on a Tapestation.
Alternatively, use an Agilent RNA 6000 pico kit if using a Bioanalyzer.
Follow the instructions carefully.
Perform the described reactions in a dedicated RNA bench that is cleaned with RNaseZap before starting procedures.
Use dedicated pipettes and tube racks that are thoroughly cleaned before experiments.
Thaw 5× Ultra Low First-Strand Buffer at 22°C.
Vortex the buffer to ensure all components are properly mixed.
Thaw nuclease free water at room temperature.
Gradually thaw on ice: 10× lysis buffer, 10× reaction buffer, 3′ SMART-Seq CDS Primer II A, and SMART-Seq v4 Oligonucleotide.
Store RNAse inhibitor and SMARTScribe Reverse Transcriptase at −20°C until use.
Place the SMARTScribe Reverse Transcriptase in a −20°C portable cooler.
Prepare a 10× Reaction buffer by mixing 19 μL of 10× Lysis buffer with 1 μL of RNase Inhibitor to a total of 20 μL.
Mix gently and spin down the reaction buffer before storing on ice.
Add samples in 0.2 mL pcr tubes (nuclease free certified).
Place the tubes on a rack on ice.
Add 2 μL of the thawed 3′ SMART-Seq CDS Primer II A (12 μM) to each tube.
Vortex gently and spin down the tubes.
Incubate the tubes at a thermocycler at 72°C for 3 min.
Ensure the lid has been preheated before starting the incubation.
Prepare the mix for cDNA synthesis reaction while the tubes are incubating.
Calculate enough volume for all samples, preparing 10% more of the total volume needed.
Immediately after completion of the 3 min incubation at 72°C, place the tubes on ice.
Incubate the tubes on ice for 2 min.
Prepare the master mix for the PCR amplification reaction.
During the 2 min incubation period, add 2 μL per reaction and 2.2% of SMARTScribe Reverse Transcriptase to the master mix.
Gently mix the reverse transcriptase enzyme before adding it to the master mix.
Spin down the mixture after addition.
Transfer 7.5 μL of the mix to each tube.
Carefully mix the content of each tube by pipetting.
Spin the tubes briefly.
Transfer tubes containing cDNA to a thermal cycle with the pre-heated lid set at 42°C.
Use the following program: (details from table:files/protocols_protocol_2145_12.csv).
Pause point: The tubes, containing cDNA, can be safely stored at 4°C or -20°C overnight.
Calculate the amount of reactions needed and prepare an additional 10% to ensure sufficient mix for all samples.
Thaw the reagents on ice.
Mix the required reagents per reaction as specified in the protocol table.
Add SeqAmp polymerase just before starting the reaction.
Pipette 30 μL of master mix into the tube containing first strand cDNA.
Mix the content of the tubes thoroughly.
Spin down the tubes to concentrate the mixture at the bottom.
Run the thermocycler program as detailed in the protocol table.
Store the tubes safely at 4°C overnight if not proceeding immediately.
Determine the optimal amount of PCR amplification cycles for your type of cells and RNA quality before proceeding with large scale experiments.
Add 1 μL of 10× lysis buffer to each reaction.
Purify the cDNA using Agencourt AMPure XP beads (Beckman).
Vortex the beads well just before use to ensure optimal dispersion.
Bring the beads to room temperature for at least 30 minutes before use.
Add 50 μL of vortexed AMPure XP beads per sample.
Mix thoroughly by pipetting up and down the entire volume of the reaction.
Let the samples stand at room temperature for 8 minutes to allow DNA binding to the beads.
Spin down the tubes and place them on a magnetic rack.
Incubate for 5 minutes to allow bead binding to the tube walls in contact with the magnet.
Remove the supernatant carefully from tubes on the magnetic stand without touching the beads.
Wash the beads with 200 μL of freshly prepared 80% ethanol.
Let the ethanol stand for around 30 seconds.
Carefully remove the ethanol, ensuring not to touch the beads.
Repeat the wash with another 200 μL of 80% ethanol.
Keep the tubes on the magnetic rack during washing.
Quickly spin down the tubes and place them back on the magnetic rack after the last wash.
Using a 20 μL tip, carefully remove residual ethanol without touching the beads.
Wait for the beads to dry for around 2 minutes.
Add 17 μL of elution buffer to the dried beads.
Resuspend the beads by pipetting up and down ten times.
Incubate at 22°C for 2 minutes to allow rehydration of the beads.
Spin down the tube.
Place on a magnet and let stand for 2 minutes.
Ensure that the supernatant appears clear.
Collect the supernatant containing amplified DNA.
Transfer the supernatant to a low binding tube.
Store the DNA at -20°C until quality control and sequencing.
Quantify the libraries.
Perform a quality control check.
Measure DNA using High Sensitivity Qubit 1x DS DNA assay with a Qubit Fluorometer.
Assess size distribution and overall quality of the library using Agilent D5000 Assay for Tapestation.
Submit the libraries to the Sequencing core facility for pooling.
Sequence the libraries using the Hiseq 4000 platform with paired-end (PE) 75 bp read lengths.
Prepare the Wash, Permeabilization, and Antibody buffers as described.
Mobilize the cells into 96-well plates.
Count the CD4 SP cells after sorting to confirm the precise number of starting material.
Transfer the required volume of cell suspension corresponding to 5*10^5 cells per sample to a nuclease-free 1.5 mL tube.
Centrifuge at 200 × g for 3 min at RT.
Carefully remove the supernatant.
Wash with 100 μL Wash Buffer per sample by resuspending the cell pellet thoroughly.
Centrifuge the tube at 200 × g for 3 min at RT.
Carefully remove the supernatant.
Repeat washing steps once more.
Add 105 μL Wash Buffer per sample to the tube and resuspend the cells thoroughly.
Split the samples into separate wells.
Aliquot 100 μL of washed cells into the wells of a 96-well U-bottom plate, each well for each antibody that will be used.
Centrifuge the plate at 453 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the cells within the wells using 50 μL cold Antibody Buffer.
Add 0.5 μg of GATA3 (clone: D13C9) XP Rabbit mAb to the corresponding sample.
Check the precise concentration of the GATA3 antibody listed in the “Certificate of analysis” on the product’s webpage.
Contact Technical support if using a previous lot of GATA3 antibody to ensure the precise concentration.
Add 0.5 μg of IgG control antibody to other samples.
Prepare 1 mg/mL working stock dilution of CUTANA rabbit IgG CUT&RUN negative control antibody in antibody buffer.
Add 0.5 μl of antibody in 50 μl antibody buffer for the negative control.
Mix each sample by gently pipetting.
Incubate the samples for 1 h at 4°C.
Centrifuge the plate at 453 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant.
Add 200 μl cold Cell Permeabilization Buffer.
Centrifuge the plate at 453 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant.
Repeat the permeabilization steps once.
Resuspend the samples in 50 μl cold Cell Permeabilization Buffer.
Mix 2.5 μL pAG-MNase to each sample.
Incubate the plate at 22°C for 10 min.
Centrifuge the plate at 453 × g for 5 min, 4°C.
Discard the supernatant.
Add 200 μl cold Cell Permeabilization Buffer.
Centrifuge the plate at 453 × g for 4 min, 4°C.
Remove the supernatant.
Resuspend the cells to 50 μl cold Cell Permeabilization Buffer.
Mix well by gently pipetting.
Place the plate on ice.
Add 1 μL Chromatin Digest Additive (provided) to each sample.
Incubate the plate for 2 h at 4°C.
Terminate the activity of pAG-MNase by adding 33 μL Stop buffer to each sample.
Mix gently by pipetting.
Add 1 μL E. coli Spike-in DNA to each sample, corresponding to 0.5 ng.
Mix by gently pipetting.
Transfer samples to 0.2 mL PCR tubes.
Spin briefly the samples to collect all residuals.
Incubate samples in a thermocycler for 10 min at 37°C.
Transfer samples to nuclease-free 1.5 mL tubes after incubation.
Centrifuge the tubes at 600 × g for 4 min at 22°C.
Transfer the supernatant, containing released DNA, to new 1.5 mL tubes.
Mix each sample with 420 μL DNA Binding Buffer.
Vortex well to mix.
Transfer the mixed sample onto a DNA cleanup column placed in a collection tube.
Centrifuge the column at 16,000 × g for 30 s at 22°C.
Discard the flow-through.
Wash the column with 200 μL DNA Wash Buffer.
Centrifuge for 30 s at 16,000 × g at 22°C.
Discard the flow-through.
Repeat washing and centrifuging twice more.
Discard the flow-through after each wash step.
Centrifuge the samples at 16,000 × g for 30 s at 22°C to completely dry the column.
Place the dried column in a new nuclease-free 1.5 mL tube.
Add 12 μL DNA Elution Buffer to the center of the column.
Incubate the samples for 5 min at 22°C.
Centrifuge at 16,000 × g for 1 min at 22°C.
Determine the concentration of small fractions of CUT&RUN DNA using a Qubit™ fluorometer.
Use 1 μL to measure the concentration (C) of the eluted DNA.
Prepare a 0.5–1 ng/μL dilution of each sample in molecular grade water using 1 μL or less if applicable.
Analyze diluted samples in the High Sensitivity D1000 ScreenTape assay.
Determine the percentage of large fractions of chromatin within each sample.
Prepare a 10 mM Tris pH 8.0 buffer by diluting 1 M Tris pH 8.0 to 1:100 in Molecular Grade Water.
Transfer 3 ng of DNA corresponding to the small fraction of DNA into a sterile nuclease-free PCR tube.
Bring the volume of the tubes to 25 μL by adding appropriate amount of 10 mM Tris pH 8.0 buffer.
Add components for end repair reaction to the tubes containing the 25 μL DNA, as specified in protocol.
Set P200 pipette to 25 μL and mix sample thoroughly by pipetting at least 10 times.
Spin tube briefly to collect all residual liquids.
Place tube in thermocycler with heated lid set to ≥ 60°C.
Run end repair program as per the protocol instructions.
Dilute Adaptor (stock 15 μM) to 1:12.5 fold in 10 mM Tris pH 8.0 to achieve 1.2 μM.
Add components for adaptor ligation to the tube containing End Prep Mixture, as specified in protocol.
Set a P200 pipette to 25 μL and then mix the sample by thoroughly pipetting (at least 10 times).
Spin briefly the tube containing the mixed sample.
Place the tube in a thermocycler with the heated lid off and incubate the sample at 20°C for 15 min.
Add 1.5 μL of USER™ enzyme to the ligation mixture.
Mix well by pipetting.
Incubate the samples at 37°C for 15 min after adding USER™ enzyme.
Fully resuspend AMPure XP beads by vortexing and equilibrate them at 22°C for at least 30 min.
Prepare fresh 80% ethanol.
Add 80 μL of AMPure XP beads to the adaptor ligation mixture.
Mix thoroughly by pipetting (at least 10 times).
Incubate the samples at 22°C for at least 5 min after adding beads.
Place the tubes on an appropriate magnetic stand to separate the beads from the supernatant.
After 5 min, carefully remove and discard the supernatant by pipetting without disturbing the beads.
Keep the tubes on the magnetic stand.
Wash the beads by adding 200 μl of freshly prepared 80% ethanol.
Incubate for 30 s at 22°C.
Carefully remove and discard the supernatant by pipetting.
Repeat the wash with ethanol.
Briefly spin the tubes, place them back on the magnet, and remove any residual ethanol with a P10 pipette without disturbing the beads.
Air-dry the beads for 5 min to ensure ethanol evaporation while the tubes are on the magnetic stand with the lid open.
Elute the DNA target by adding 15 μl of 10 mM Tris pH 8.0.
Mix well by pipetting at least 10 times or by vortexing.
Incubate the samples for at least 2 min at 22°C.
Perform a quick spin to collect all residual liquids.
Place the tubes on a magnetic stand.
After 5 min, carefully transfer 13 μl to a new sterile PCR tube.
Prepare the PCR reaction for the enrichment of the adaptor-ligated DNA.
Set a P200 pipette to 25 μL to mix the sample thoroughly by pipetting at least 10 times.
Spin briefly the tubes.
Place the tubes in the thermocycler.
Run the PCR program as specified.
If starting material is 1 ng of DNA, increase the number of cycles to 14.
Vortex AMPure XP beads to resuspend and incubate them at 22°C for at least 30 min.
Prepare fresh 80% ethanol.
Add 30 μL (1.0× ratio) AMPure XP beads to the adaptor ligation mixture.
Mix well by pipetting at least 10 times.
Incubate the samples at RT for at least 5 min.
Place the tubes on an appropriate magnetic stand to separate the beads from the supernatant.
After 5 min, carefully remove and discard the supernatant by pipetting without touching the beads.
Keep the tubes on the magnetic stand.
Add 200 μL of 80% freshly prepared ethanol to wash the beads and incubate for 30 s at 22°C.
Carefully remove and discard the supernatant by pipetting without disturbing the beads.
Repeat the wash with 80% ethanol twice.
Remove any residual ethanol after the last wash.
Briefly spin the tubes and place them back on the magnet to remove ethanol residues with a P10 pipette.
Air-dry the beads for 5 minutes while the tubes are on the magnetic stand with the lid open.
Resuspend the beads without over drying, ensuring no apparent cracking of the beads.
Remove the tubes from the magnetic stand.
Add 15 μL of 10 mM Tris pH 8.0 to elute the DNA target.
Thoroughly resuspend the beads by pipetting at least 10 times for efficient elution of DNA.
Let the samples stand for at least 2 minutes at 22°C.
Perform a quick spin to collect the beads at the bottom of the tube.
Place the tubes on a magnetic stand and wait for 5 minutes or until the solution is clear.
Carefully transfer 13 μL from each tube to new sterile 0.2 mL PCR tubes, avoiding touching the beads.
Quantify the library using 1 μL with the Qubit 1x HS DNA assay in a Qubit™ fluorometer.
Prepare a 0.5–1 ng/μL dilution of each library in molecular grade water using 1 μL or less if applicable.
